If the skill isn't installed yet, the fix is to install it (a separate prework step), not to point at a path.' The worked example ('Invoke the access-control-analysis skill on the feature I'll name.') invokes by name only, no path.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chain by back-reference + deterministic path, never invented alias.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The 'Chain back-reference' entry (L295–299) states: 'Refers to an earlier artifact by both anchor (*the file you just created*) and path (`notes/X.md`)... Together they survive both same-session continuity and cross-session resumption.' The worked example carries both an anchor ('the test-strategy skill we just wrote') and enough deterministic grounding (named feature, named ADR) to resolve — matches the rule's two-part shape.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Append-vs-integrate — name integration mode on regeneration with new context source.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The 'Integration mode' entry (L109–113) states the rule directly: 'Names whether the new input rewrites *through* the existing artifact or *adds a new section* to it... *Integrate, not append* tells it the new input reshapes the whole... No middle ground. The unspoken default is always *append*.' Matches §12's core claim (default is append; name the mode explicitly) and its worked example quotes the exact 'integrate, don't append' phrasing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Citation discipline — extend cite-or-flag scope + quote supporting sentence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The 'Source-or-flag' entry (L273–277) states: 'Every claim cites the file or page it came from. If you can't cite, mark `[NOT FOUND]` and don't fill from prior knowledge... The flag turns gaps into evidence the human can act on rather than hidden fabrication.' Its worked example ('If you can't find a source for a claim, write "[NOT FOUND]", do not fill from prior knowledge') matches §13(a)'s cite-or-flag mechanic; the entry doesn't claim to cover §13(b)'s narrower quote-the-supporting-sentence sub-case, which is a reasonable simplification for a one-move catalogue entry, not a misstatement of what it does cover.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Question-dump default — `in turn` too soft; two legal shapes.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The 'Batched, not dumped' entry (L219–223) states: 'Asked for *the questions you need to encode the skill,* the agent posts a seven-question list and you answer two before drifting. *Ask one at a time* installs conversational rhythm. *Three at a time* trades some rhythm for batch efficiency.' This matches §15's shape (a) almost exactly (structural one-or-N-at-a-time prompting), and the worked example ('Ask one question, wait for my answer, then ask the next. Don't show me the next question until I've answered the previous one.') is shape (a) verbatim in spirit.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Preamble before action — design around it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The 'Preamble suppressor' entry (L181–185) states: 'Claude defaults to two-to-four sentences of preamble before producing anything. Plan mode is the worst case: the highest-attention slot at the top of the response... gets eaten by narration. *No preamble. Lead with the diff* doesn't kill the habit but bites it down to something you can skim past.' This matches §17's current (2026-09-03-narrowed) framing exactly — plan-mode as the live structural trigger, suppressor-phrasing as one legal fix — and doesn't claim the retired 4+-substep trigger anywhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Self-critique register, not defense, when Claude interrogates own work.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The 'Self-critique register' entry (L235–239) states the rule directly: 'Uses self-critique verbs (*re-read, audit, find what's still surface*). Never defense verbs (*defend, justify, prove*)... *Defend* primes Claude's helpful-advocate mode and produces rationalisations.' Matches §18 verbatim in substance, including the same worked contrast (self-critique surfaces gaps, defense surfaces excuses).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Grill before save — collaborative quality at artefact assembly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The compendium was narrowed 2026-09-03 (dated the same day as this file's most recent Quality audit): 'the benefit is unevidenced... this never gates and rarely fires... Raise §20 only where a run actually showed a downstream re-run caused by a gap.' The 'grill-before-save' three-move pattern entry on this page (L342–347) still frames the pattern as firing generically 'when an artifact needs cross-examination before it persists', with no hint that §20's own compendium now treats reaching for this shape by default as unevidenced. The entry is descriptive of two real, already-shipped exercises (`push-back-on-the-plan-2`, `diagnose-and-resend-6`), so it isn't factually wrong — but a reader skimming this catalogue for a template to reach for when authoring a NEW artifact-assembly exercise would come away thinking 'grill before save' is a default move to add, exactly the instinct the 2026-09-03 narrowing was written to head off. Low harm (descriptive naming, not a live prompt this page ships), so non-blocking.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Add a half-clause to the grill-before-save entry noting the move is confirmed-by-evidence-only now (point at §20), or leave the entry purely descriptive of the two named exercises without generalising 'fires when' language a future author could read as a green light.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Module names in prompt prose are fine — they ground the session.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The 'Multi-result fallback' entry's worked example (L287) quotes: '...Pick the one whose log includes the 'M4 starting point' commit. If that commit message has been rewritten, ask me for the SHA.' — uses the module-numbered commit message purely as an in-session artifact reference (grounding a git-log search), exactly the sanctioned shape §32 describes, not a dangling reference to a curricular event with no in-session referent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Git-output greps asserting exact-N need multi-result fallback.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The 'Multi-result fallback' entry (L283–287) states the rule directly and names the exact failure modes §33 lists: 'a push leaves both `m4/<slug>` and `remotes/origin/m4/<slug>`, and a replay can leave several... Pick the one whose log includes the 'M4 starting point' commit. If that commit message has been rewritten, ask me for the SHA.' Matches shape (B) from §33 (prompt inline-handles the multi-result case) precisely.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguation, anchors, and decision logic that bind Claude live INSIDE prompt fence.
